summary: Prepared GAIA is the most mature variant, featuring a complete stack with FastAPI, Streamlit, and SQLite persistence. It includes data anonymization and automated tests, though it suffers from a significant bug in its startup script and a lack of API authentication.

findings.description: Sensitive medical data is accessible via public API endpoints without any authentication.
findings.evidence: GET /reports endpoint in api/main.py returns all extracted data from SQLite without credentials check.

findings.description: The startup script run_system.py uses blocking subprocess.run() calls, preventing the parallel execution of the API and Dashboard.
findings.evidence: subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "uvicorn", ...]) in start_api_server() blocks execution before start_admin_dashboard() is called.

findings.description: Implemented data anonymization logic to remove sensitive identifiers like PESEL numbers from user input.
Comprehensive suite of unit tests covering system initialization, validation, and database setup.
Includes a Streamlit-based admin dashboard for health authorities to visualize reports.

missing_requirements: Dostępność: While the system architecture supports 24/7 access, the blocking bug in run_system.py makes initial deployment of both components difficult.
implementation_risks: Exposure of PII if the anonymization logic fails or is bypassed.
Unauthenticated access allows malicious actors to read or modify (if POST /query is abused) health data.
The blocking subprocess calls mean the dashboard won't start unless the API server is manually moved to background or run separately.
